the_defect.summary: verticals/mainline/apps/demo-api/src/mainline_demo_api/db.py:309 opens every production connection with row_factory=dict_row. reads.py and health.py were written to that convention (row["name"]). scenario.py, gate_run.py, transitions.py and refusal.py were not. Unpacking a dict yields its KEYS, so scenario.resolve()'s eight-name unpacking made check_id the literal seven-character string "check_id", which was then bound as $2 of _RECEIPT_SQL and rejected by the type parser one statement later.
the_defect.why_it_surfaced_as_a_500_and_not_a_TypeE: A dict of eight entries unpacks into eight names without complaint. Nothing raises at the unpacking. The wrong values travel one statement further and fail as a data error, which is why the symptom (22P02 on a uuid parameter) names a column the caller never supplied.
the_defect.why_no_test_caught_it: verticals/mainline/apps/demo-api/tests/test_gate_run.py:249 and :256 open connections with psycopg.connect(w4_database, autocommit=False) - psycopg's default tuple_row. The production path and the test path used different row factories, so the one contract that spans them was never asserted by anybody. A suite that only ever runs under one factory is what created this defect; that is why the new test asserts BOTH.

the_fix.shape: scenario.positional(conn, sql, params) - a two-line helper that sets the row factory on the CURSOR rather than on the connection. psycopg's own mechanism: the statement declares the shape it is written against instead of inheriting one from whoever opened the connection.
the_fix.why_not_flip_db_py: db.py:309's dict_row serves reads.py's 43 row["name"] accesses across the twelve GET resources and health.py's five. Flipping it would trade one broken endpoint for thirteen. db.py and reads.py were not edited.
the_fix.why_not_mutate_conn_row_factory_in_passi: a warm Lambda container reuses one connection across invocations, so a gate run that left the connection on tuple_row would break every GET served after it. positional() mutates nothing; tests/test_row_factory_contract.py::test_positional_does_not_mutate_the_connection_it_was_handed asserts that.
the_fix.where_the_helper_lives: scenario.py, because it is the module gate_run.py and transitions.py both already import - the only shared root of the three, since gate_run imports scenario and transitions imports both. Three copies of a two-line helper would be three places for it to drift.
the_fix.secondary_hardening: gate_run._fingerprint's zip over _FINGERPRINT_TABLES was strict=False and is now strict=True, with an explicit None guard on the row. A silently truncated zip is how a collapsed row would have produced a persistence check that under-reports the tables it claims to cover.

resolution.by: W1 of the demo-correctness wave (docs/leads/demo-correctness-plan.md), owner of refusal.py
resolution.summary: The single positional row access at refusal.py:235 is gone, and the property that made it possible - a statement inheriting whatever row factory opened the connection - is gone from the whole file rather than from the one line that crashed.

the_fix.shape: the same remedy the other three modules use - scenario.positional(conn, sql, params), which sets row_factory=tuple_row on the CURSOR and mutates nothing about the connection, so reads.py still receives dicts on the same warm container.
the_fix.why_the_four_no_row_statements_were_rout: SAVEPOINT, ROLLBACK TO and RELEASE return no rows, so none of them could be misread today. They go through the helper anyway because the property being removed from this module is INHERITING A FACTORY, not CRASHING. A later edit that adds a RETURNING clause to one of them must not be able to reintroduce the defect quietly.
the_fix.why_not_row['explain_refusal']: Keying the row by the column name would also have stopped the KeyError, and would have made refusal.py depend on a name CockroachDB chose for it. The sibling statements prove that is not safe: measurement_that_decided_the_fix_shape above records gate_run._FINGERPRINT_SQL returning ten columns all named `count`, of which a dict row keeps one. The test therefore runs the same call under an alias and requires the same answer, so the fix cannot silently become a name dependency.
the_fix.the_savepoint_fence_is_unchanged: _explain is called three times inside the one transaction gate_run holds open across four beats, and 0119a raises rather than emit a plausible reason set. The fence's four statements are the same four, in the same order, with the same control flow; only the cursor they run on changed.
the_fix.one_docstring_correction_made_in_passing: the module docstring said `All six statements this module issues`. There are five. Corrected to five rather than left as a number a reader could not reproduce by counting.

the_test_that_was_missing_for_this_file.design: every claim is made twice - once through db.connection() (the REAL production factory; a hand-rolled psycopg.connect(..., row_factory=dict_row) would only assert that the file agrees with itself) and once through an explicit tuple_row connection - and the two answers are then required to be EQUAL.
the_test_that_was_missing_for_this_file.the_negative_control: two halves, because one alone would prove the wrong thing. test_the_decomposition_column_is_named_after_the_function reads cursor.description off refusal._EXPLAIN_SQL itself and FAILS if the column is ever renamed, so the measured premise this whole artefact rests on cannot drift silently. test_the_answer_does_not_depend_on_that_column_name then runs the same call with `AS renamed_on_purpose` and demands an identical answer, which is what proves refusal.py does not depend on the name the first test pins.
the_test_that_was_missing_for_this_file.both_branches_of_explain_are_covered: epoch_pin_permit reaches the decomposition and RETURNS a payload - the branch that carried the defect - and gate_closed_when_issued against a permit whose projected counter is zero RAISES P0001, which is the branch the SAVEPOINT exists for. Asserting only the branch that was broken would leave the other free to break next.
two_properties_a_fix_could_have_destroye: test_the_savepoint_fence_survives_a_raise_inside_one_open_transaction - three _explain calls in one transaction, the middle one raising, and the transaction still usable afterwards
test_building_a_refusal_leaves_the_connection_handing_out_dicts - a warm container's next GET must still get dicts, which is what fails if a fix mutates conn.row_factory in passing
the_test_that_was_missing_for_this_file.structural_ratchet_over_this_one_file: test_no_statement_in_refusal_inherits_the_connection_s_row_factory walks the AST and bans conn.execute(...).fetch*(). Deliberately narrower than the package-wide ratchet: the behavioural tests only cover the statements a refusal happens to reach, and a statement added to refusal.py tomorrow would be covered by nothing until this fails. test_the_production_module_still_routes_through_positional is its complement - a ratchet that only bans a shape is satisfied by deleting the statement, so the replacement is required to be present.
